title: SLO breakpoint mapping for multimodal endpoints with tiered circuit-breakers and regional choreography
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
Define, implement, and operationalize per-endpoint and per-model SLO/SLI breakpoints for multimodal routes (text/chat/embedding/image features) that drive a unified, tiered circuit-breaker and regional failover choreography. This ticket focuses on formalizing metric definitions, burn-rate thresholds, and the automatic actions (local shed -> model downgrade -> regional failover -> graceful degrade responses) mapped to error-budget breakpoints.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- A canonical SLI bundle per route type (chat, text-generation, embeddings, multimodal image features) with measurement windows and cardinality guidance.
- Error-budget breakpoints (green/yellow/orange/red) per model variant and per-traffic class (interactive vs batch).
- A deterministic mapping from breakpoint to actions: (1) enqueue/backpressure tuning, (2) soft shed prefixes (best-effort), (3) model downgrade to quantized/cheaper variant, (4) cross-region failover to warm region, (5) synthetic "degraded response" template when all fallbacks exhausted.
- Implement telemetry: dashboards for per-model burn-rate, rolling-1h/6h/7d SLIs, and a compact incident playbook view.
- Create a rollout and validation plan (canary + shadow) with test prompts and failure-injection harness.

Proposed SLI definitions (high-level):
- Availability: successful inference responses with HTTP 200 and non-empty model output. Measured as percentage over 5m/1h/7d windows.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 from request arrival to first-token emitted for streaming routes and to final token for non-streaming. Separate windows per interactive/batch.
- Correctness (optional safelist): model-ended-with-error vs model-response-with-high-likelihood-of-dont-fulfill. For now this is treated as a secondary SLI to track quality regressions, not primary load triggers.

Error-budget breakpoints (example):
- Green: burn-rate <= 1.0 (no action)
- Yellow: 1.0 < burn-rate <= 4.0 -> raise priority on autoscaler, increase soft-queue depth, enable prefix caching aggressive TTL.
- Orange: 4.0 < burn-rate <= 10.0 -> begin model variant downgrade (to quantized variant / smaller context config), enable selective shedding for long-context requests, tighten rate-limits for anonymous plans.
- Red: burn-rate > 10.0 -> regional circuit-breaker: reject new requests locally and route to next-best region or fallback model; trigger on-call and start customer communications flow.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Strict p99 SLOs will cause frequent orange/red actions under taily LLM workloads; we prefer burn-rate driven actions focusing on p95 and availability for interactive routes.
- Model downgrade risks quality regressions; therefore all downgrades must be tied to a rapid A/B quality monitor and automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold.
- Regional failover increases cross-region egress cost and latency; mapping prioritizes customers with enterprise-tier traffic-tagging and routes low-tier traffic to cheaper fallbacks.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec & schema (this ticket): finalize SLI definitions, measurement windows, and breakpoint mappings; add SLO metadata to model registry entries.
2) Telemetry & dashboards: build burn-rate panels, per-model heatmaps, and a compact playbook view in Console.
3) Orchestration hooks: expose a declarative SLO policy object (yaml/json) that runtime can read to enact actions. Implement in runtime-1.20.
4) Failover choreography: implement region routing priorities and safe-traffic drain mechanics.
5) Canary rollout: internal + opt-in customers, run synthetic traffic and failure-injection scenarios.

Artifact links and checkpoints:
- Draft spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/SLO+Breakpoints+and+Tiered+CB (internal)
- Design PR for SLO schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1298
- Telemetry dashboard drafts: Console -> Observability -> SLO Burn Rates (link: internal dashboard id 7842)
- Failure-injection harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reliability-chaos (branch: slo-breakpoints)

Risks & mitigations:
- False-positive shedding: mitigate by using tiered thresholds and short probation windows, and by shadow-testing actions before reject-paths.
- Observability blind spots for multimodal endpoints: add tag-based sampling to capture large-image requests and heavy-context chat sessions.
- Customer surprise during rollouts: plan opt-in canaries and customer communication templates for enterprise customers.

Next steps:
- Review with Runtime and Console leads (scheduled 2026-02-22).
- Finalize SLI measurement queries and push to metrics repo.
- Implement SLO metadata push in model onboarding pipeline (ENG task).
